chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Khallad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Regarding a man who slaughtered a dove from the doves of the Sanctuary (Al-Haram): He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is the expiation.' I said: 'So can he eat it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No.' I said: 'Can he throw it away?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Then there would be another expiation upon him.' I said: 'So what should he do with it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should bury it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling and procedure for a dove from the Haram if it is slaughtered?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the specific legal consequences for slaughting the sacred doves of Mecca, emphasizing the preservation of their sanctity through burial rather than consumption or casual disposal. It highlights the Shia juristic principle that improper handling of the sacrificed animal incurs additional liability, reflecting the broader Quranic emphasis on respecting the symbols of God.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Khallad, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>

having said regarding a man who slaughtered a dove from the doves of the Al-Harram. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Upon him is the expiation’. I said, ‘So can he eat it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No?’ I said, ‘Can he throw it away?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Then there would happen to be another expiation upon him’. I said, ‘So what should he do with it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should bury it’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Khallad who has said the following:

“About a man who has slaughtered a pigeon of the pigeons of al-Haram (the sacred area) abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘He owes a ransom.’ I then asked, ‘Can he use it for food?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘No, he cannot do so.’ I then asked, ‘Can he throw it away?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘If he did so he will owe another ransom.’ I then asked, ’What then he must do?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘He is required to bury it.’”
